title: China's Astribot Raises Fourth Round in Six Months, Valuation Jumps to 15 Billion Yuan
key_facts: On 13 Oct 2026 Astribot announced a new funding round of 1 billion yuan (about $149.4 million), lifting its valuation to 15 billion yuan (about $2.2 billion).
The round was led by Toukong Donghai (Shenzhen Investment Holdings), with Hongtai Fund, Ninghai Xingtaihe Fund and Shanheng Capital, and an extra investment from existing shareholder Xianmu.
It is Astribot's fourth round in about six months (Series A+, A++, B and this one) and comes about three months after the June 2026 Series B, when its valuation first passed 10 billion yuan.
Astribot says the money goes to model iteration, hiring, commercialisation and production capacity.
Its T1 humanoid began shipping in June 2026 at around 90,000 yuan (about $13,000), and combined S and T series capacity has reached the 10,000-unit level, according to the company.
Customers named include Golden Horse, ThunderSoft, Seer Robotics, CCTV and JD.com; home products are still in research and development.
quote_evidence: On October 13, the company announced the completion of a new 1 billion yuan (approximately $149.4 million) funding round, lifting its valuation to 15 billion yuan (approximately $2.2 billion).
This marks Astribot's fourth funding round in roughly six months.
Combined production capacity for the S and T series has now reached the 10,000-unit level.
why_it_matters_hint: Four rounds in six months and state-backed funds in the mix show how fast money is flowing to Chinese humanoid makers.
